title: The beach, theirs
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · the aggregator
logline: Wednesday. The beach with nobody on it in spring, which hasn't happened since 2006. The pup and Wood and the drift log. The strip is quietly, guiltily glad, and draws the gladness in the light.

panels.composition: The beach, March noon, empty to the horizon. WOOD on the drift log. BARNABY II at the tideline. The light kind.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a beach at noon empty to the horizon with a man on a bleached drift log and a small three-legged dog at the tideline, kind light, no words

panels.composition: Wood's face. The thing he's not supposed to feel. Drawn.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, close-up of a man's face showing a quiet guilty contentment, no words
image.notes: The strip lets him feel it and doesn't forgive or condemn.

panels.composition: The pup running the whole beach. Nobody to avoid. The prints, two-one, from one end to the other.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a small three-legged dog running the full length of an empty beach leaving a two-one trail of prints, no words

panels.composition: The log. The man. The dog back, wet. The beach theirs. Nobody says whose it usually is.

notes: Wordless. The gladness drawn in the light.
